Letting the weight drop at the bottom.
Using your shoulders for momentum.
pupm.p: Very safe and easy to load progressively. Ideal for getting close to failure on the last sets.

curlinv.e: Standing, bar held overhand, palms facing the floor, hands shoulder-width apart. Elbows pinned to your sides, curl the bar to your shoulders keeping your wrists in line with your forearms, then lower slowly.
err: Bending the wrists down.
Swinging the torso.
Using your regular curl weight: it will be much lower.
curlinv.p: Strengthens the forearms and brachialis, often forgotten. Useful if your grip gives out before your back on pulls.

drag.e: Standing, bar in an underhand grip against your thighs. Instead of curling the bar in an arc, drag it up along your torso by pulling your elbows back, up to your lower chest. Lower it the same way.
err: Letting the bar drift away from the body.
Shrugging toward the ears.
Going too heavy and pulling with the back.
drag.p: By pulling the elbows back, you take the shoulder out of the movement and hit the biceps differently. Keep it as a curl variation, not a main lift.

martx.e: Standing, dumbbells by your sides, palms facing your thighs. Curl one dumbbell diagonally toward the opposite shoulder, without rotating your wrist, then lower and alternate with the other arm.
err: Swinging the torso to cross farther.
Lifting the elbow off your side.
Switching arms too fast.
martx.p: A hammer curl variation that emphasises the brachialis. Do all the reps on one side before switching if you lose control.

tricor.e: Facing a high pulley, rope in hand, elbows pinned to your sides, torso leaning slightly. Push the rope down until your arms are straight, spreading the ends at the bottom, then come back up until your forearms pass horizontal.
err: Letting the elbows move forward and up.
Leaning over the weight to push with your body weight.
Coming up too high, past the elbows.
tricor.p: Spreading the rope at the bottom gives a fuller contraction than with a bar. Sets of 10 to 15 at the end of the workout.

skull.e: Lying on a bench, EZ bar held with arms straight above your chest. Bend only your elbows to lower the bar toward your forehead or just behind your head, then straighten your arms again.
err: Flaring the elbows outward.
Moving the arms during the descent, which turns it into a press.
Lowering too fast near your face.
skull.p: The angled bar protects the wrists. If your elbows creak, lower the bar behind your head rather than toward your forehead.

extdb.e: Standing, one dumbbell held with both hands overhead, arms straight. Abs tight, lower the dumbbell behind your head by bending your elbows, which stay pointed at the ceiling, then press back up.
err: Arching the lower back.
Letting the elbows flare.
Cutting the descent behind the head short.
extdb.p: With the arms overhead, the triceps' long head is stretched: it's what gives the arm its size. Sit down if you arch.

pompt.e: In push-up position, hands under your shoulders or slightly narrower. Lower keeping your elbows tucked against your torso, going back, until you brush the floor, then push by fully straightening your arms.
err: Flaring the elbows, which hands the work back to the chest.
Letting the hips sag.
Bringing the hands so close it hurts the wrists.
pompt.p: Triceps with no equipment. Too easy beyond 20 reps: add weight on your back or raise your feet.

trim.e: Seated, elbows on the pad, aligned with the machine's pivot. Straighten your arms fully while contracting your triceps, then return slowly until your forearms pass a right angle.
err: Lifting the elbows off the pad.
Setting the seat without aligning the elbow with the pivot.
Letting the weight come back all at once.
trim.p: Guided and easy to dose: a good choice to finish the workout close to failure safely.

trinv.e: Facing a high pulley, straight bar held palms up. Elbows pinned to your sides, push the bar down to straight arms, then come back up slowly without lifting your elbows.
err: Using your regular-grip weight: the underhand grip is weaker.
Letting the wrists bend backward.
Moving the elbows forward.
trinv.p: The reverse grip shifts the emphasis on the triceps. Alternate it with the regular pushdown from week to week.

bfronth.e: Lying on a bench, a dumbbell in each hand, arms straight above your chest, palms facing each other. Bend your elbows to lower the dumbbells beside your head, then straighten your arms.
err: Letting the elbows flare outward.
Moving the shoulders.
Clanking the dumbbells at the top.
bfronth.p: A neutral grip that's gentler on the elbows than the bar. Ideal if you train with dumbbells only.

elskull.e: Lying on a bench, band anchored low and secure behind your head. Arms pointing toward the ceiling, elbows bent, extend your forearms to vertical, then return slowly.
err: Letting the elbows drift backward.
Letting the band snap back.
Anchoring the band too high, which removes the tension.
elskull.p: The band is hardest at the end of the movement, where the triceps is strongest. Sets of 15 to 20.

dcd.e: Lying on the decline bench, legs secured, shoulder blades squeezed. Lower the bar to your lower chest, elbows at 45°, then press straight up to straight arms.
err: Bouncing off the chest.
Flaring the elbows to 90°.
Relaxing the shoulder blades.
dcd.p: A shorter range than the flat bench press, often better tolerated by the shoulders. As with the bench, keep two reps in reserve without a spotter.

dhd.e: Lying on a decline bench, legs secured, a dumbbell in each hand above your chest. Lower the dumbbells to the sides of your lower chest, elbows at 45°, then press while bringing them slightly together.
err: Letting the dumbbells go too low.
Flaring the elbows to 90°.
Sitting up abruptly from the decline bench with the dumbbells.
dhd.p: Rest the dumbbells on your thighs before lying down and getting up. The angle targets the lower chest.

dcsm.e: Bench placed so the bar comes down over your lower chest. Shoulder blades squeezed, unrack the bar, lower it to your chest, elbows at 45°, then press to straight arms.
err: Placing the bench too high or too low under the bar.
Forgetting to re-rack at the end of the set.
Letting the elbows flare.
dcsm.p: The rails secure the bar: you can get closer to failure than on the free bench press. The load isn't comparable to a free bar.

dcism.e: Bench inclined at 30° under the Smith machine, bar lined up with your upper chest. Unrack, lower the bar to your upper chest under control, then press to straight arms.
err: Inclining the bench beyond 45°, which turns it into a shoulder exercise.
Lifting your hips off the bench.
Bouncing at the bottom.
dcism.p: Handy for targeting the upper chest without a spotter. Progress in small 2.5 kg steps.

chpi.e: Seated with your back well supported, handles at upper chest height. Press forward and up until your arms are almost straight, then return slowly until you feel your chest stretch.
err: Setting the seat too high or too low.
Lifting your back off the backrest.
Letting the weight slam at the end of the return.
chpi.p: Being guided, it lets you push hard on the upper chest without managing balance. A good alternative to the incline press.

pompl.e: Hands well wider than your shoulders, core braced from heels to head. Lower until your chest nears the floor keeping your elbows at about 60°, then push without breaking the line of your hips.
err: Placing the hands so wide the elbows flare to 90°.
Letting the hips sag.
Cutting the descent short.
pompl.p: Puts more emphasis on the chest than regular push-ups. Add weight on your back when 20 reps come out.

pompi.e: Hands on a bench, box or bar, body in a plank. Lower your chest toward the support keeping your elbows going back, then push to straight arms.
err: Breaking the body line at the hips.
Placing the hands too far in front of the shoulders.
Going too fast.
pompi.p: The easy version of push-ups: the higher the support, the easier it is. Lower it over the weeks until you reach push-ups on the floor.

ecpb.e: Flat bench between two low pulleys, a handle in each hand, arms above your chest, elbows slightly bent. Open your arms in an arc until you feel the stretch, then close while squeezing your chest.
err: Bending the elbows on the way down, which turns it into a press.
Lowering the arms below the bench.
Clanking the handles at the top.
ecpb.p: The cables keep tension at the top, where dumbbells have none left. Sets of 12 to 15.

ecpi.e: Bench inclined at 30° between two low pulleys. Arms open, elbows slightly bent, bring the handles over your upper chest in an arc, then lower slowly.
err: Inclining the bench too steeply.
Bending and straightening the elbows during the movement.
Letting the shoulders roll forward at the end of the movement.
ecpi.p: Targets the upper chest with constant tension. Do it after an incline press.

eldc.e: Lying on a bench, band passed under the bench or behind your back, a handle in each hand at chest height. Press toward the ceiling until your arms are straight, then lower slowly.
err: Letting the elbows flare to 90°.
Letting the band snap back on the way down.
Choosing a band that's too weak for the last reps.
eldc.p: The band gets harder at the end of the movement. Double it or use a thicker one when you go past 20 reps.

dhn.e: Lying on a bench, dumbbells held palms facing each other, pressed together above your chest. Lower keeping your elbows close to your torso until you touch your chest, then press.
err: Flaring the elbows.
Letting the dumbbells come apart on the way down.
Bouncing off the chest.
dhn.p: The neutral grip is the gentlest on the shoulders and works the triceps more. A good option if your shoulder bothers you.

dmsm.e: Seated on an upright bench under the Smith machine, bar in front of your face at chin height. Press straight up until your arms are straight, then lower back to chin level.
err: Lowering the bar behind the neck.
Lifting your back off the backrest.
Placing the bench too far back.
dmsm.p: Being guided, it lets you press heavy without a spotter. Keep the bench positioned so the bar comes down in front of your face.

dmhd.e: Standing, dumbbells at shoulder height, palms facing forward. Squeeze your glutes and abs, press the dumbbells straight up until your arms are straight, then lower to ear height.
err: Arching the lower back.
Pushing the dumbbells forward.
Bending the legs to help.
dmhd.p: Standing, your core works along with your shoulders. Go 10 to 20% lighter than seated.

elfp.e: Back to a low pulley, handle between your legs, arm straight. Raise your arm in front of you to eye level, then lower slowly.
err: Swinging the torso.
Raising higher than your head.
Bending the elbow.
elfp.p: The front delts already work a lot on presses: keep this light and occasional.

oisc.e: Facing a pulley at shoulder height, rope in hand, arms straight. Pull the rope toward your face while spreading your elbows at shoulder height, squeeze your shoulder blades, then return slowly.
err: Letting the elbows drop below the shoulders.
Pulling with your torso by leaning back.
Shrugging.
oisc.p: Close to the face pull, with more emphasis on the rear delts. Sets of 12 to 20.

oisi.e: Lying face down on a slightly inclined bench, a light dumbbell in each hand, arms hanging. Raise your arms out to the sides to horizontal, elbows slightly bent, then lower slowly.
err: Going too heavy and pulling with the back.
Lifting the chest off the bench.
Raising the hands higher than the elbows.
oisi.p: The bench prevents any cheating: the rear delts work alone. Very light dumbbells are enough.

eli.e: Lying on your side against an incline bench, dumbbell in the top hand, arm hanging in front of you. Raise your arm out to the side to vertical, then lower slowly.
err: Rotating the torso to help.
Bending the elbow on the way up.
Going too heavy.
eli.p: Lying down, tension is highest at the bottom, where the standing raise has almost none. One arm at a time.

cuban.e: Standing, light dumbbells in hand. Raise your elbows out to the sides to shoulder height, rotate your forearms up without dropping your elbows, then press overhead. Come back in reverse.
err: Using dumbbells that are too heavy.
Letting the elbows drop during the rotation.
Rushing without marking each step.
cuban.p: A shoulder health exercise, not a strength one. Two to five kilos, as a warm-up or at the end of the workout.

rotp.e: Standing side-on to a pulley at elbow height, handle in the far hand. Elbow pinned to your side and bent at 90°, rotate your forearm outward, then return slowly.
err: Lifting the elbow off your side.
Rotating the torso to help.
Going too heavy.
rotp.p: Strengthens the small muscles that stabilise the shoulder. RPE 6 maximum, 15 to 20 reps.

kbdma.e: Standing, two kettlebells in the rack position. Press one kettlebell overhead until your arm is straight, lower it, then go with the other arm, core tight.
err: Leaning the torso to the opposite side.
Arching the lower back.
Bending the wrist backward.
kbdma.p: Alternating demands more core stability than pressing with both arms. If it's too heavy, start with a single kettlebell.

eloi.e: Band anchored in front of you at shoulder height, one end in each hand, arms straight. Spread your arms out to the sides while squeezing your shoulder blades, then return slowly.
err: Bending the elbows to make it easier.
Shrugging.
Letting the band snap back.
eloi.p: Rear delts at home. Sets of 15 to 25, step back to increase the tension.

tpsu.e: Seated under the high pulley, bar held palms toward you, hands shoulder-width apart. Torso leaning slightly back, pull the bar to your upper chest leading with your elbows down, then return to straight arms.
err: Leaning far back to pull.
Pulling with the arms and forgetting the back.
Coming back up too fast.
tpsu.p: The underhand grip works the biceps more: it's the cable version of chin-ups.

tp1.e: Seated or kneeling under a high pulley, handle in one hand, arm straight. Pull your elbow toward your hip keeping your torso still, then return slowly until you feel your back stretch.
err: Rotating the torso to pull.
Pulling toward the shoulder rather than the hip.
Cutting the return short.
tp1.p: Working one side at a time fixes imbalances between your two lats. Start with the weaker side.

tbtc.e: Facing a high pulley, rope in hand, arms straight in front of you, torso leaning slightly. Bring the rope down to your thighs in an arc, elbows almost locked, spreading the ends at the bottom, then let it rise slowly.
err: Bending the elbows.
Leaning further and further.
Letting the weight shoot back up.
tbtc.p: The rope lets you go further at the bottom than the bar. Sets of 12 to 15.

tps1.e: Seated facing the low pulley, feet braced, handle in one hand, arm straight. Torso upright, pull your elbow back along your side while squeezing your shoulder blade, then return slowly.
err: Twisting the torso to swing the weight.
Rounding the back on the return.
Shrugging the shoulder toward the ear.
tps1.p: One arm at a time for a bigger range and better feel in your back.

rwsu.e: Standing, bar held palms facing forward, hands shoulder-width apart. Bend your torso to 45°, back flat, knees slightly bent. Pull the bar to your lower belly keeping your elbows close to your body, then lower under control.
err: Standing up on each rep.
Rounding the lower back.
Pulling toward the chest instead of the belly.
rwsu.p: The underhand grip recruits the lower lats and biceps more. Keep the same flat back as in the regular row.

rwhm.e: Seated, chest against the pad, handles held with arms straight up and forward. Pull your elbows down and back while squeezing your shoulder blades, then return slowly.
err: Lifting the chest off the pad.
Pulling with the biceps.
Letting the weight come back all at once.
rwhm.p: Halfway between a vertical and a horizontal pull: a good complement in a back workout.

tbarp.e: Lying face down on the inclined pad, handles in hand, arms straight. Pull the handles toward your chest while squeezing your shoulder blades, then lower slowly.
err: Lifting the chest off the pad.
Cutting the descent short.
Shrugging.
tbarp.p: The pad removes all stress from the lower back. Ideal if your lower back bothers you.

kbrw2.e: Standing, torso bent at 45°, back flat, a kettlebell in each hand, arms straight. Pull your elbows toward your hips while squeezing your shoulder blades, then lower slowly.
err: Rounding the back.
Standing up to pull.
Pulling toward the shoulders.
kbrw2.p: Two kettlebells at once also train your back's holding strength. Keep your knees slightly bent.

seal.e: Lying face down on an incline bench, bar held under the bench, arms straight. Pull the bar up while squeezing your shoulder blades until it touches the underside of the bench, then lower slowly.
err: Lifting the chest off the bench.
Pulling with the arms without squeezing the shoulder blades.
Dropping the bar.
seal.p: No cheating possible: a strict row with no stress on the lower back.

landr.e: Bar wedged in a corner or landmine holder, loaded at the other end. Standing side-on, torso bent, grab the bar near the plates with one hand. Pull toward your hip, then lower slowly.
err: Rotating the torso.
Rounding the back.
Pulling toward the shoulder.
landr.p: The bar's arc is natural for the shoulder. Switch sides each set.

sqh.e: Standing, a dumbbell in each hand by your sides, feet shoulder-width apart. Descend by pushing your hips back and your knees in line with your feet, to parallel, then stand up by pushing through your heels.
err: Letting the knees cave inward.
Rounding the back at the bottom.
Heels lifting.
sqh.p: The squat when you only have dumbbells. When your grip gives out before your legs, move to the goblet squat or lunges.

ferh.e: Standing, dumbbells in hand. Take a long step back and lower until your back knee nearly touches the floor, torso upright. Push through your front heel to come back, then switch legs.
err: Taking too short a step.
Letting the front knee cave inward.
Leaning the torso forward.
ferh.p: Stepping back rather than forward spares the knees. It's the lunge to choose if forward lunges bother you.

montb.e: Bar on your upper back, facing a knee-height bench or box. Put your whole foot on the bench and step up by pushing through that heel, without help from the other leg. Lower slowly.
err: Pushing off with the back leg.
Choosing a bench that's too high.
Letting the knee cave in.
montb.p: Works each leg separately. Do all the reps on one leg before switching.

lext1.e: Seated at the machine, back supported, roller on the lower shin of one leg. Straighten the leg fully while squeezing the quad, pause, then lower slowly.
err: Kicking to lift the weight.
Lifting your hips off the seat.
Letting the weight drop.
lext1.p: Useful to catch up a weaker quad. Always start with the weaker leg.

sql.e: Bar on your upper back, feet well wider than your shoulders, toes turned out. Descend pushing your knees in line with your feet, torso upright, to parallel, then come up.
err: Letting the knees cave in.
Leaning the torso forward.
Going lower than your hips allow.
sql.p: The wide stance shifts work toward the glutes and adductors. A good variation of the regular squat.

lcas.e: Seated at the machine, roller under your calves, thighs locked by the pad. Bend your knees all the way, pause, then come back up slowly until your legs are almost straight.
err: Setting the thigh pad too loose.
Cutting the return short.
Going too fast.
lcas.p: Seated, the hamstrings are stretched: it's the most effective leg curl version for building muscle.

lcd.e: Standing at the machine, roller behind one ankle, hips against the pad. Bend your knee to bring your heel toward your glutes, then lower slowly.
err: Arching the back to lift.
Lifting the hip off the pad.
Swinging the leg.
lcd.p: One leg at a time to fix an imbalance. Sets of 10 to 15 per leg.

revhyp.e: Lying face down on the machine, hips at the edge, legs hanging. Raise your straight legs to horizontal while squeezing your glutes, then lower under control.
err: Swinging the legs for momentum.
Going above horizontal by arching.
Letting the legs drop.
revhyp.p: Strengthens the lower back without compressing it. Start unloaded, 15 to 20 reps.

kickpc.e: On all fours, hands under your shoulders, knees under your hips. Push one leg back and up keeping the knee bent, until your thigh lines up with your back, then lower.
err: Arching the lower back.
Rotating the pelvis to the side.
Going too fast.
kickpc.p: Glutes with no equipment. Add an ankle weight or a band when 20 reps come out.

addp.e: Side-on to a low pulley, strap on the nearest ankle. Hold the machine and bring the leg across in front of the other, then return slowly.
err: Leaning the torso to compensate.
Going too fast.
Going too heavy.
addp.p: An alternative to the adductor machine. Sets of 12 to 15 per leg.

bulsm.e: Smith machine bar on your upper back, one foot forward, the other resting behind on a bench. Lower straight down until your front thigh is parallel to the floor, then come up.
err: Placing the front foot too close.
Letting the front knee cave in.
Pushing off with the back leg.
bulsm.p: The rails remove the balance challenge: you can load more than with dumbbell Bulgarian split squats.

molah.e: Seated on a bench, ball of one foot on a plate, dumbbell resting on the knee. Lower your heel as far as possible, then rise as high as you can onto your toes.
err: Bouncing at the bottom.
Cutting the range short.
Going too fast.
molah.p: Seated, it's the soleus that works. Pause for one second at the bottom of each rep.

molab.e: Seated on a bench, balls of your feet on a plate, bar resting on your knees with a towel. Lower your heels as far as possible, then rise onto your toes.
err: Bouncing at the bottom.
Lifting the toes off the support.
Going too fast.
molab.p: The barbell equivalent of the seated calf machine. Sets of 15 to 20.

shrp.e: Facing a low pulley, bar in hand, arms straight. Raise your shoulders toward your ears as high as possible, pause, then lower slowly.
err: Rolling the shoulders.
Bending the elbows.
Going too fast.
shrp.p: The cable keeps tension at the bottom. Sets of 12 to 15 with a pause at the top.

tirh.e: Standing, dumbbells in front of your thighs, palms toward you. Pull the dumbbells up along your body, leading with your elbows, to chest height, then lower slowly.
err: Raising the elbows above the shoulders.
Swinging the torso.
Going too heavy.
tirh.p: Dumbbells leave the wrists free, which is easier on the shoulders than the bar. Stop the pull at chest height.

situp.e: Lying down, knees bent, feet on the floor, hands on your temples. Curl your torso up until you're sitting, then lower slowly one vertebra at a time.
err: Pulling on the neck.
Dropping back down.
Throwing the torso up with the arms.
situp.p: Beyond 20 reps, hold a plate against your chest.

crm.e: Seated at the machine, handles in hand, feet braced. Curl your torso toward your knees by contracting your abs, then return slowly.
err: Pulling with the arms.
Going too fast.
Letting the weight come back all at once.
crm.p: Easy to load progressively, like any other muscle. Sets of 10 to 15.

crinvp.e: Lying on the floor, feet toward a low pulley, straps on your ankles. Knees bent, bring your knees toward your chest by lifting your pelvis, then lower slowly.
err: Swinging the legs.
Not lifting the pelvis.
Letting the legs drop.
crinvp.p: The loaded version of the reverse crunch. Control the descent over two seconds.

flh.e: Standing, a dumbbell in one hand, the other hand on your head or hip. Lean toward the dumbbell side, then come back up by contracting the opposite obliques.
err: Leaning the torso forward.
Holding a dumbbell in each hand, which cancels out the effort.
Going too fast.
flh.p: One dumbbell at a time. Do all the reps on one side, then switch.

buch.e: Side-on to a high pulley, handle held with both hands, arms straight. Pull the handle diagonally toward the opposite knee by rotating your torso and hips, then return slowly.
err: Pulling with the arms.
Bending the elbows.
Rounding the back.
buch.p: The rotation comes from the torso and hips. Sets of 10 to 15 on each side.

crd.e: Lying on a decline bench, feet secured, hands on your temples. Curl your upper torso toward your knees, then lower without fully resting your shoulders.
err: Pulling on the neck.
Lifting the whole torso.
Dropping down.
crd.p: Harder than the floor crunch. Increase the bench angle to progress.

rjb.e: Lying on a bench, hands gripping behind your head, legs straight. Raise your legs to vertical while slightly lifting your pelvis, then lower slowly without touching the floor.
err: Arching the lower back at the bottom.
Swinging the legs.
Lowering too fast.
rjb.p: More accessible than hanging leg raises. Bend your knees if your lower back arches.

crx.e: Lying down, knees bent, hands on your temples. Curl your torso while rotating to bring your elbow toward the opposite knee, which comes up to meet it. Lower and alternate.
err: Pulling on the neck.
Moving only the elbow without rotating the torso.
Going too fast.
crx.p: Works the obliques. Keep a slow pace.

velocr.e: Lying down, hands on your temples, legs off the floor. Bring one elbow toward the opposite knee while straightening the other leg, then alternate as if pedalling.
err: Pedalling fast without rotating the torso.
Pulling on the neck.
Arching the lower back.
velocr.p: Count one rep per side. Going slowly makes the exercise much more effective.

jack.e: Lying down, arms straight behind your head, legs straight. Raise your arms and legs at the same time to touch your feet above your hips, then lower slowly.
err: Bending the knees.
Dropping back down.
Arching the lower back.
jack.p: Demanding: if you can't manage 8 reps, do reverse crunches first.

crobl.e: Lying on your side, legs bent and stacked, top hand on your temple. Lift your torso sideways by contracting your obliques, then lower.
err: Pulling on the neck.
Rolling onto your back.
Going too fast.
crobl.p: Do all the reps on one side before switching.

talons.e: Lying down, knees bent, feet on the floor, shoulder blades lifted. Lean to one side to touch your heel with your hand, then the other side, without resting your shoulders.
err: Resting the shoulders between reps.
Pulling with the neck.
Going too fast.
talons.p: Simple and effective for the obliques. Count one rep per side.

tuck.e: Seated on the edge of a bench, hands at your sides, torso leaning back, legs straight. Bring your knees toward your chest while slightly straightening your torso, then extend your legs again.
err: Putting the feet on the floor between reps.
Rounding the back.
Going too fast.
tuck.p: Accessible and effective. Hold a dumbbell between your feet when 20 reps come out.

rintel.e: Band anchored at elbow height to your side, on the side of the working arm. Elbow pinned to your body and bent at 90°, forearm turned outward. Bring your forearm across to your belly without lifting the elbow, then return slowly.
err: Lifting the elbow off the body to help the movement.
Rotating the torso instead of turning the shoulder.
rintel.p: The partner of external rotation: train both directions to balance the shoulder. Light resistance, 15 to 20 reps, two seconds on the way back.

rintp.e: Seated or standing side-on to a pulley set at elbow height. Elbow bent at 90° and pinned to your side, bring the handle to your belly by rotating the shoulder, then return under control.
err: Going too heavy: these are small muscles.
Letting the elbow drift away from the body.
rintp.p: Stay around RPE 6, 15 clean reps. The goal is shoulder tolerance, not performance.

oisrot.e: Torso bent over or supported on an incline bench, a very light dumbbell in each hand. Raise your arms out to the sides, then rotate your forearms up at the end of the movement, as if showing your palms in front of you. Return slowly.
err: Using dumbbells that are too heavy and losing the rotation.
Shrugging toward the ears.
oisrot.p: One or two kilos are enough. It's a control exercise: 12 to 15 slow reps.

cbras.e: Standing, arms straight out to the sides at shoulder height. Draw circles, small at first and then bigger and bigger, forward and then backward.
err: Shrugging during the circles.
Going fast instead of looking for range.
cbras.p: An ideal warm-up before an upper-body workout: 15 circles in each direction.

batep.e: Standing, a stick or towel held with both hands, wide grip. Arms straight, bring the stick over your head and behind you, then back to the front, without bending your elbows.
err: Using too narrow a grip and forcing the movement.
Arching the lower back to gain range.
batep.p: Narrow your grip by just a few centimetres once the pass-through feels easy.

tdm.e: Standing, a stick held behind you with both hands, palms facing back. Gently move the stick away from your back while keeping your torso upright, until you feel the stretch at the front of your shoulders. Hold while breathing.
err: Leaning the torso forward to lift higher.
Bouncing into the stretch.
tdm.p: Thirty seconds, twice. Useful after a pressing workout.

bcrois.e: Standing, bring one straight arm across your chest and gently pull it toward you with the other hand, above the elbow. Keep the shoulder down and hold.
err: Pulling on the elbow joint itself, which stresses it.
Letting the shoulder rise toward the ear.
bcrois.p: Thirty seconds per side. Simple and effective at the end of a workout.

chq.e: On all fours, hands under shoulders, knees under hips. Lift one knee and draw a big circle with it, forward, out to the side and back, without moving your pelvis or back.
err: Rotating the pelvis along with the leg.
Going fast and shrinking the range.
chq.p: Ten circles per side in each direction. Excellent before a leg workout.

chd.e: Standing, one hand on a support. Raise one knee in front of you, open it out to the side, then lower the leg, drawing the biggest possible circle with the knee. Then switch direction.
err: Leaning the torso to compensate.
Making a small circle for lack of control.
chd.p: Ten circles per leg in each direction. Keep your pelvis facing forward.

groin.e: In a push-up position, arms straight. Bring one foot next to the hand on the same side, let the hip sink for a moment, then bring the leg back and alternate.
err: Rounding the back to bring the foot forward.
Raising the hips too high.
groin.p: Eight per side. If your foot doesn't reach your hand, place it as far forward as you can: it will come.

fig4.e: Lying on your back, rest one ankle on the opposite knee. Grab the thigh of the supporting leg and pull it toward you until you feel the stretch in the glute of the crossed leg.
err: Lifting the head and tensing the neck.
Letting the crossed knee drift back to the middle.
fig4.p: Thirty seconds per side. Gently push the crossed knee outward to deepen it.

addet.e: Lying on your side, head on your arm. Raise your top leg toward the ceiling while opening it, and hold it with your hand if you can, until you feel the stretch on the inside of the thigh.
err: Rolling backward to lift higher.
Bending the knee a lot, which loses the stretch.
addet.p: Thirty seconds per side. A strap around the foot helps if your hand can't reach.

flexd.e: In a lunge, back foot on the ball of the foot. Tuck your pelvis by squeezing the back glute, then gently shift your weight forward until you feel the stretch at the front of the back hip.
err: Arching the lower back instead of tucking the pelvis.
Taking too short a lunge.
flexd.p: Thirty seconds per side. Raise the arm on the stretched side to deepen it.

hext.e: Standing facing a support, band around the ankle and anchored low in front of you. Push your straight leg back while squeezing the glute, without arching your back, then return slowly.
err: Arching the lower back to go further.
Leaning the torso forward.
hext.p: Twelve to fifteen reps per leg. The movement is small: the glute does the work, not the back.

hflex.e: Standing with your back to the anchor, band around the ankle. Raise your knee in front of you to hip height, pause, then lower slowly.
err: Leaning back to raise the knee.
Letting the leg drop.
hflex.p: Twelve reps per leg. Strengthening the hip flexors often makes them less stiff than only stretching them.

bascp.e: Lying on your back, knees bent. First press your lower back into the floor by tucking your pelvis, then peel your spine off one vertebra at a time up into a bridge. Come down by rolling through in reverse.
err: Lifting as one block without rolling the spine.
Arching at the top of the bridge.
bascp.p: Ten slow reps. It's a control exercise: the slower, the better.

gpoit.e: Lying on your back, bring both knees to your chest and wrap your arms around them. Relax your shoulders and breathe, letting your lower back round gently.
err: Lifting the head and tensing the neck.
Pulling hard on the knees.
gpoit.p: Thirty seconds, breathing slowly. Good relief after a long day sitting.

croix.e: Lying face down, arms out in a cross. Raise one heel toward the ceiling and bring it toward the opposite hand by rotating your pelvis, shoulders on the floor, then return and alternate.
err: Lifting the shoulders off the floor.
Forcing the rotation in jerks.
croix.p: Eight per side, slowly. Don't go further than your back accepts without pain.

torsal.e: Lying on your back, arms out in a cross. Bring one bent knee up and let it fall across to the other side of your body, keeping both shoulders on the floor. Turn your head the other way and breathe.
err: Lifting the opposite shoulder to go lower.
Forcing the knee to the floor with your hand.
torsal.p: Thirty seconds per side. Let gravity do the work.

cgen.e: Standing, feet together, knees slightly bent, hands on your knees. Draw small circles with your knees, one way and then the other.
err: Forcing big ranges.
Locking the knees straight.
cgen.p: Ten circles in each direction, as a gentle warm-up.

sqas.e: Standing, feet hip-width apart, arms straight in front. Slowly squat down to a depth that stays comfortable for your knees, then stand up. Knees in line with your feet.
err: Letting the knees cave inward.
Going lower than the knee tolerates.
sqas.p: Twelve slow reps. Increase the depth from session to session, as long as the knee stays calm.

quadet.e: Lying on your side, grab your top ankle and bring your heel toward your glute. Tuck your pelvis to feel the stretch at the front of the thigh, without arching.
err: Arching the lower back.
Letting the knee drift up and out.
quadet.p: Thirty seconds per side. More comfortable than standing when balance or the knee is an issue.

cchev.e: Standing on one leg or seated, toes on the floor or in the air. Draw big circles with your ankle, one way and then the other.
err: Moving the whole leg instead of the ankle.
Going too fast.
cchev.p: Ten circles in each direction for each foot.

molmur.e: Hands against a wall, one leg straight behind with the heel down, the other bent in front. Move your hips toward the wall until you feel the stretch in the back calf.
err: Lifting the back heel.
Turning the back foot outward.
molmur.p: Thirty seconds per leg. The back foot stays straight, pointing at the wall.

sole.e: Standing, one foot in front of the other, both knees bent. Shift your weight onto the back leg keeping the heel down, until you feel the stretch low in the calf, near the heel.
err: Straightening the back knee, which stretches the gastrocnemius instead.
Lifting the heel.
sole.p: Thirty seconds per leg. Complements the straight-leg stretch.

cpoi.e: Arms straight in front or out to the sides, fists closed or hands open. Draw circles with your wrists, one way and then the other.
err: Moving the whole arm.
Going too fast.
cpoi.p: Ten circles in each direction, before any push or pull workout.

avbet.e: Kneeling, hands on the floor, fingers pointing toward your knees. Gently sit your hips back toward your heels keeping your palms down, until you feel the stretch in your forearms.
err: Lifting the palms off the floor.
Bouncing into the stretch.
avbet.p: Thirty seconds. Start with fingers pointing sideways if it's too intense.

mentp.e: Seated or standing, hands clasped behind your head. Let the weight of your hands gently bring your chin toward your chest, without pulling, and breathe.
err: Pulling with the arms.
Rounding the whole back instead of the neck.
mentp.p: Twenty seconds, twice. Let go as soon as the stretch gets strong.

nuqinc.e: Standing, one hand on the side of your head. Gently tilt your ear toward your shoulder while letting the other shoulder drop, until you feel the stretch on the side of the neck.
err: Raising the shoulder toward the ear.
Pulling hard on the head.
nuqinc.p: Twenty seconds per side. Ideal after a day at a screen.

hdos.e: Standing, hands clasped in front of you, arms straight at shoulder height. Push your hands far forward while rounding your upper back and spreading your shoulder blades, head between your arms.
err: Rounding the lower back instead of the upper back.
Shrugging.
hdos.p: Thirty seconds. Breathe into your upper back to open it further.

rotbu.e: Standing, hands on your hips, pelvis still. Slowly rotate your torso to one side and then the other, as far as you can without moving your hips.
err: Rotating the pelvis with the torso.
Using momentum.
rotbu.p: Ten rotations per side. Keep your knees slightly bent to lock the pelvis.

trneg.e: Get above the bar with a box or a jump, chin over the bar. Then lower yourself as slowly as possible, 4 to 5 seconds, down to straight arms.
err: Dropping at the end of the descent.
Jumping too high and letting the shoulders go loose.
trneg.p: The gateway to your first pull-up. Once you can hold 5 descents of 5 seconds, try a full rep.

mup.e: Hanging from the bar (or rings), pull explosively to the chest, roll the torso over the bar, then press to straight arms. Lower under control.
err: Pulling only to the chin: the transition needs a very high pull.
Getting over one arm at a time with a twist.
mup.p: Prerequisites: 10 clean pull-ups and 10 dips. Train explosive chest-to-bar pull-ups and deep dips first.

tr1.e: Hang from one hand, the other free or on your chest. Brace and pull until your chin reaches the hand, then lower slowly.
err: Spinning the whole body to help.
Helping with the other hand on the wrist.
tr1.p: Advanced skill. Build up with weighted pull-ups, archer pull-ups and one-arm negatives.

hpike.e: Hang with straight arms, legs straight and together. Curl the pelvis and raise your feet to touch the bar, then lower without swinging.
err: Swinging with the whole body.
Bending the knees to cheat at the top.
hpike.p: Progress from knee raises to legs at 90° first. Ten strict reps is a very good level.

pomp1.e: Feet wide, one hand under the shoulder, the other behind your back. Brace hard, lower the chest close to the floor, then press without twisting.
err: Opening the hip and twisting the body.
Only going down a few centimetres.
pomp1.p: Start with the hand on a bench, then lower the height. Archer push-ups are a good in-between step.

pompp.e: In push-up position, lower then push hard enough for the hands to leave the floor. Land with slightly bent arms and go again.
err: Landing with locked elbows.
Letting the hips sag on landing.
pompp.p: Few reps, all fast. Add a clap once the push is well controlled.

pompgl.e: Do a push-up, then on the way up rotate onto one arm into a side plank, top arm to the ceiling. Return and alternate sides.
err: Letting the hip drop in the side plank.
Rotating before finishing the push-up.
pompgl.p: Eight per side. A good drill to link pushing and core work.

splsq.e: One foot forward, the other far behind on the toes. Lower the back knee towards the floor with an upright torso, then drive up through the front foot.
err: Feet on the same line, which kills balance.
Letting the front knee cave in.
splsq.p: Twelve per leg. Next, back foot on a bench (Bulgarian split squat) or jump squats.

jsq.e: Squat down, then jump as high as you can, extending the legs. Land softly on the balls of your feet and flow into the next squat.
err: Loud landing with straight legs.
Knees caving in on landing.
jsq.p: Ten quality jumps beat thirty sloppy ones. Rest fully between sets.

ktj.e: Standing, jump and bring your knees up to your chest, land softly with bent knees and go again right away.
err: Leaning forward instead of lifting the knees.
Landing heels first.
ktj.p: Short sets of 8 to 10. Great at the end of a street session for conditioning.

trxrow.e: Short straps, handles in hand, walk your feet in and lean back, arms straight, body braced. Pull your chest to the handles squeezing your shoulder blades, then lower slowly.
err: Letting the hips sag.
Shrugging as you pull.
trxrow.p: 3 to 4 sets of 8 to 15. The further your feet walk under the anchor, the harder it gets.

trxrows.e: Lie under the anchor, straps set so that straight arms lift you off the floor, heels down, body straight. Pull your chest up to the handles, elbows close, then lower under control.
err: Bending at the hips instead of staying straight.
Pulling with the arms without squeezing the shoulder blades.
trxrows.p: 3 sets of 6 to 12. The hardest TRX row: body almost horizontal.

trxpu.e: Facing away from the anchor, handles in hand, walk your feet back and lean forward, arms straight, body braced. Lower your chest between the handles keeping the straps steady, then press back up.
err: Letting the straps drift apart.
Arching the lower back.
trxpu.p: 3 to 4 sets of 8 to 15. The more you lean, the harder it is; the unstable straps work the stabilisers.

trxfly.e: Facing away from the anchor, arms straight in front, elbows slightly bent. Open your arms in an arc as you lean forward, then bring them back together squeezing your chest.
err: Bending the elbows like a push-up.
Going too deep and straining the shoulders.
trxfly.p: 3 sets of 8 to 12, with little lean at first: it gets hard fast.

trxy.e: Facing the anchor, leaning back, arms straight in front. Raise your arms into a Y overhead squeezing your shoulder blades, body braced, then return slowly.
err: Bending the elbows.
Arching the back to come up.
trxy.p: 3 sets of 10 to 15 with a small lean. Great for posture and shoulder health.

trxt.e: Facing the anchor, leaning back, arms straight in front. Open your arms out to the sides into a T squeezing your shoulder blades, then return under control.
err: Pulling with the biceps.
Letting the hips sag.
trxt.p: 3 sets of 10 to 15. Pair it with the Y-raise for the upper back.

trxfp.e: Facing the anchor, leaning back, arms straight. Pull the handles to either side of your face, elbows high, rotating your hands back, then return slowly.
err: Elbows too low.
Pushing the head forward to the handles.
trxfp.p: 3 sets of 12 to 15 with a slight lean. A classic to balance out push-ups.

trxcu.e: Facing the anchor, leaning back, arms straight, palms up. Bend your elbows to bring the handles to your forehead, elbows fixed at shoulder height, then lower slowly.
err: Letting the elbows drop.
Using the hips.
trxcu.p: 3 sets of 10 to 15. Walk your feet closer to the anchor to make it harder.

trxtri.e: Facing away from the anchor, leaning forward, arms straight overhead. Bend only the elbows to bring your hands to your forehead, then straighten to come back.
err: Flaring the elbows.
Moving at the shoulders instead of the elbows.
trxtri.p: 3 sets of 10 to 15, with a small lean at first.

trxsq.e: Facing the anchor, handles in hand, arms straight. Squat down using the straps to keep your chest up and go deeper, then stand back up.
err: Pulling hard with the arms to stand up.
Letting the knees cave in.
trxsq.p: 3 sets of 12 to 20. Perfect to learn a deep squat.

trxpis.e: Facing the anchor, handles in hand, on one leg with the other straight in front. Sit down on the standing leg using the straps for help, then stand back up.
err: Heel lifting off.
Knee caving in.
trxpis.p: 3 sets of 5 to 8 per leg. The straps are an aid: use them as little as you can.

trxss.e: Facing away from the anchor, one foot in both cradles behind you. Lower on the front leg until the thigh is parallel to the floor, then drive up through the heel.
err: Front knee travelling far forward.
Pushing with the back leg.

trxlc.e: On your back, heels in the cradles, hips up. Pull your heels towards your glutes keeping the hips high, then straighten the legs slowly.
err: Letting the hips drop.
Rushing the way back.

trxhb.e: On your back, heels in the cradles, knees bent. Lift your hips until knees, hips and shoulders line up, squeeze your glutes, then lower.
err: Arching the lower back at the top.
Pushing through the toes.
trxhb.p: 3 sets of 12 to 15. Do it on one leg to make it harder.

trxfo.e: Facing away from the anchor, leaning forward, arms straight. Let your arms rise in front as your braced body falls forward, then pull them back under your shoulders squeezing your abs.
err: Arching the lower back.
Bending the elbows.
trxfo.p: 3 sets of 8 to 12. The more you lean, the harder it gets.

trxpl.e: Feet in the cradles, on your forearms, body straight from heels to shoulders. Hold without letting the straps swing.
err: Hips too high or too low.
Holding your breath.
trxpl.p: 3 sets of 20 to 45 s. Harder than a floor plank: the straps move.

trxkt.e: In a straight-arm plank, feet in the cradles. Pull your knees to your chest rounding your back, then extend your legs back to the plank.
err: Letting the hips drop on the way back.
Hands too far ahead of the shoulders.

trxpk.e: In a straight-arm plank, feet in the cradles. Lift your hips to the ceiling with straight legs into an inverted V, then lower back to the plank.
err: Bending the knees.
Shoulders drifting behind the hands.
trxpk.p: 3 sets of 8 to 12. The advanced version of the knee tuck.

trxmc.e: In a straight-arm plank, feet in the cradles. Drive your knees to your chest one after the other, fast, keeping the hips low.
err: Hips rising.
Straps swinging.

trarch.e: Wide grip, pull your chin towards one hand while the other arm stays almost straight, like a bowstring. Lower under control, then switch sides.
err: Bending the straight arm: it turns into an off-centre regular pull-up.
Swinging to reach the hand.
trarch.p: A step towards the one-arm pull-up: once 3 × 6 per side is clean, let the straight arm help less and less.

trmix.e: One hand overhand, the other underhand, hands shoulder-width apart. Pull your chest to the bar without twisting, lower to straight arms. Swap hands every set.
err: Torso rotating towards the underhand side.
Always the same hand in front.
trmix.p: Add weight once 3 × 8 is clean; it is good groundwork for the one-arm pull-up.

trlest.e: Weight on a dip belt or in a tight backpack. Start from straight arms with shoulders engaged and pull until your chin clears the bar, no swing.
err: Weight swinging and giving momentum.
Half reps at the bottom.
trlest.p: Start with 5 kg once you reach 12 clean pull-ups; add 2.5 kg when you hit 3 × 6.

pompis.e: Hands close together on a bench or low bar, body braced. Lower with elbows tucked along your sides, then press to straight arms.
err: Elbows flaring out.
Hips breaking the line.
pompis.p: Lower the support over the weeks, then move to close-grip push-ups on the floor.

pomph.e: After each push-up, walk your hands one notch around a circle centred on your feet, like a clock hand. One lap one way, then the other.
err: Letting the hips sag while moving.
Shortened push-ups to go faster.
pomph.p: Add a clap to the move once a full lap is easy.

pompeg.e: Wide hands, lower to the bottom, then shift your chest towards one hand as the other arm straightens, come back to the centre and go to the other side before pressing up.
err: Pushing up between sides.
Hips up to make it easier.
pompeg.p: A step towards archer and one-arm push-ups: keep more and more of your weight on the bent arm.

dipan.e: Supported on the rings, arms straight and rings turned out. Lower until your shoulders are below the elbows, keeping the rings tight to your body, then press up.
err: Rings drifting away from the body.
Going too deep without control.
dipan.p: Prerequisite: 15 bar dips. Start with a support hold, 3 × 20 s.

pistol.e: On one leg, the other straight in front, arms forward for balance. Sit down until your hips are near the heel, heel on the floor, then stand up without bouncing.
err: Heel lifting off.
Knee caving inwards.
pistol.p: Start holding a post or sitting down to a bench; remove the help once 3 × 5 per leg is clean.

stepg.e: Whole foot on a bench, step up by driving through the heel and raise the other knee to hip height at the top. Step down slowly, same leg for the whole set.
err: Pushing off the trailing leg.
Leaning far forward.
stepg.p: Raise the box height, then add a weighted backpack.

fsaut.e: From a lunge, jump up and switch legs in the air. Land softly straight into the next lunge.
err: Back knee slamming the floor.
Landing on straight legs.
fsaut.p: Jump higher first, then add reps.

bondl.e: From one leg, bound sideways and land on the other leg with a soft knee. Hold for a second, then go back the other way.
err: Knee caving on landing.
Chaining without sticking the landing.
bondl.p: Increase the distance, then chain them without pauses once landings are solid.

grenou.e: Squatting with hands behind your head, jump forward and land straight back into the squat. Chain the hops.
err: Landing on your toes without absorbing.
Rounded back at the bottom.
grenou.p: Increase the distance of each hop before adding more.

sautl.e: Feet hip-width apart, swing your arms, dip and jump as far as you can. Land flat-footed with soft knees and walk back.
err: Landing on straight legs.
Chaining jumps without rest: this is power work.
sautl.p: Measure your best jump and try to beat it; 4 to 6 jumps per set are enough.

spider.e: From a low push-up position, crawl forward bringing one knee to the elbow on the same side, opposite hand forward. Keep your body close to the floor.
err: Hips high.
Rushing and losing core tension.
spider.p: Go further, then slow down to stay low for longer.

ciseaux.e: Lying down, lower back pressed to the floor, straight legs lifted. Cross and uncross your legs in small movements without letting your lower back arch.
err: Lower back lifting off.
Legs too high: it gets too easy.
ciseaux.p: Lower your legs closer to the floor, then go longer.

legpi.e: Lying down with hands under your hips, pull your knees to your chest lifting the pelvis, then straighten your legs without touching the floor.
err: Swinging the legs.
Feet touching the floor between reps.
legpi.p: Then move on to knee raises on dip bars, and hanging.

crsusp.e: Holding a chin-up with your chin over the bar, bring your knees up to your elbows, then lower the legs without letting the arms straighten.
err: Arms straightening during the crunch.
Legs swinging.
crsusp.p: Hold the top position longer, then straighten your legs out in front.
